chunk_findings.detail:
The regression test still does not exercise the starred-unpacking false positive it claims to guard. `_worktree_change(repo, "src/mod.py", "a = range(3)
", "*a, = range(3)
")` always produces the deleted non-comment body `-a = range(3)`; the original buggy classifier already treated that removed non-comment line as code and returned False, so the test passes on the unfixed code for the wrong reason. A case that would actually fail under a `*`-as-comment classifier is one where the removed line is also comment-shaped, e.g. `# old note
` -> `*a, = range(3)
`, or where the changed content is otherwise only an added star-leading line. The classifier rewrite does not answer this: the test file still contains the same non-reproducing base/head pair.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_trivial_tier.py:test_a_starred_unpacking_change_is_not_trivial

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding #1 still holds. The current diff keeps `and not diff_is_trivial(it, cfg, repo, paths)` at line 233, before the existing `and not (not reviewed and repo is not None)` guard on the following lines. The triage says “probe: code rewritten,” but that rewrite has not moved or guarded this call: for a non-doc task with `repo=None` and `reviewed=False`, the old code would reach the `repo is not None` guard and return without doing repository work; the new code first calls `diff_is_trivial(it, cfg, None, paths)`, which is the new git-inspecting classifier, so it fails before the guard that exists to handle this `repo=None` path.
